title: Post-1947 Uprising: Colonial Repression and Nationalist Suppression
notes: Well-documented. Nationalist leaders imprisoned/exiled after the 1947 uprising; MDRM dissolved 1947; leaders sentenced to death/life imprisonment. Repression through early 1950s is confirmed.

title: Forced Labor Formally Abolished in French Madagascar
notes: Forced labor was formally abolished across French Union in 1946 (not 1952), though enforcement was inconsistent. No corroboration found for a specific 1952 prestation abolition event. The broader claim about economic coercion continuing is plausible but the specific 1952 date and 'prestation' framing could not be confirmed.

title: Loi Cadre Grants Madagascar Internal Autonomy
notes: Confirmed. Loi-cadre enacted June 23, 1956. Tsiranana's Social Democratic Party (PSD) won territorial elections. Provincial assemblies and Grand Council established.

title: Madagascar Votes to Join French Community as Autonomous Republic
notes: Confirmed. September 28, 1958 referendum. Malagasy Republic proclaimed October 14, 1958. Tsiranana headed provisional government.

title: Madagascar Achieves Full Independence from France
notes: Confirmed. Full independence June 26, 1960. Tsiranana as president. No armed conflict.

title: Tsiranana Government Suppresses Political Opposition
notes: Broadly confirmed. Tsiranana progressively restricted opposition and operated as a dominant-party state. Specific details about 1962 as the year of key restrictions are consistent with the historical record.

title: Cyclone Edith Devastates Northeast Coast and Rice Paddies
notes: No corroboration found for a Cyclone Edith striking Madagascar in early 1963. Could not confirm the name, year, or specific casualty figures.

title: Madagascar Joins Organisation of African Unity
notes: Year is wrong by more than 1 year. The OAU was founded May 25, 1963, and Madagascar signed the charter August 10, 1963. Madagascar was a founding member in 1963, not 1964.

title: Southern Drought Triggers Famine in Grand Sud Region
notes: Southern Madagascar's chronic drought vulnerability is well-documented, but no specific 1970 famine event could be confirmed from available sources. The 1971 revolt sources reference drought but focus on 1971, not 1970.

title: Peasant Revolt and Urban Labor Strikes Challenge Tsiranana Rule
notes: Confirmed. April 1971 MONIMA armed uprising in Androy led by Monja Jaona. Government suppressed it harshly (45 killed, 847 detained). Urban strikes and student protests also confirmed.

title: May Revolution Overthrows Tsiranana, Ends First Republic
notes: Confirmed. Mass protests from May 1972. Tsiranana transferred power to General Ramanantsoa. Demands included end of French neocolonial dominance.

title: French Cooperation Accords Renegotiated, Military Expelled
notes: Confirmed. Ramanantsoa government renegotiated the French cooperation accords, expelled French military, and withdrew from the Franc Zone.

title: Malagasization of Education System Implemented
notes: Confirmed. Ramanantsoa government replaced French with Malagasy as primary medium of instruction. Rapid implementation created teacher shortages and quality decline.

title: Ratsiraka Seizes Power and Declares Socialist Revolution
notes: Confirmed. Colonel Ratsimandrava assassinated February 11, 1975 after just 6 days in office. Ratsiraka selected head of state June 15, 1975; confirmed by referendum December 21, 1975. Boky Mena published. Democratic Republic of Madagascar proclaimed.

title: Socialist Nationalizations Sweep Banks and Key Sectors
notes: Confirmed. Ratsiraka nationalized banks, insurance, and key export sectors under his socialist program.

title: Forced Agricultural Cooperatives Cause Rice Production Collapse
notes: Confirmed. Socialist cooperative farming policy implemented. Rice production decline and food shortages are well-documented consequences.

title: First IMF Structural Adjustment Program Forces Liberalization
notes: Confirmed. Madagascar signed its first IMF/World Bank structural adjustment program in the late 1970s requiring liberalization in exchange for emergency loans.

title: Socialist Economic Model Collapses, GDP Contracts Sharply
notes: Confirmed. Madagascar experienced one of sub-Saharan Africa's worst economic performances in this period. GDP per capita fell sharply under combined effects of failed socialist policies and oil price shocks.

title: Export Processing Zone Legislation Attracts Garment Investors
notes: Confirmed. EPZ legislation passed mid-1980s, attracting Asian garment manufacturers. Eventually employed over 100,000 workers.

title: Cyclone Kamisy Kills Over 300 in Northwest Madagascar
notes: Year is wrong by 1 year. Cyclone Kamisy struck April 1984, not 1985. Death toll was approximately 68 overall (not over 300). Hit Mahajanga (Majunga) in northwest — region is correct.

title: National Environment Action Plan Launched with World Bank
notes: Confirmed. Madagascar's National Environment Action Plan launched in partnership with World Bank in the late 1980s, positioning Madagascar as a conservation leader.

title: Pro-Democracy Movement Mounts Mass Protests Against Ratsiraka
notes: Confirmed. Broad pro-democracy movement (Forces Vives) with unions, churches, civil society mobilized from 1990. Massive Antananarivo demonstrations forcing Ratsiraka to negotiate.

title: Bloody Saturday: Presidential Guard Massacres Protesters
notes: Confirmed. August 10, 1991 march on Presidential Palace. Presidential guard fired on crowd. Death toll disputed: government said 11, other sources range 10-130. At least 30 deaths are a reasonable figure. Event fundamentally delegitimized Ratsiraka.

title: New Democratic Constitution Adopted, Third Republic Established
notes: Confirmed. New constitution approved August 1992 referendum. Third Republic established with multi-party democracy.

title: Albert Zafy Wins First Competitive Presidential Election
notes: Confirmed. Zafy won second round February 10, 1993 with 66.74%. First genuine multi-party presidential contest. Judged free and fair.

title: Cyclone Geralda Devastates Vanilla Plantations in Northeast
notes: Cyclone Geralda struck January/February 1994 and caused extensive crop damage. However, the primary documented impacts were in Toamasina (east coast), not the Sava vanilla region specifically. Death toll was 231, not 70. The vanilla-specific claim and '70 people' figure could not be confirmed.

title: President Zafy Impeached by National Assembly
notes: Confirmed. Zafy impeached July 26, 1996 by National Assembly (99 of 134 deputies in favor). High Constitutional Court upheld September 4, 1996.

title: Ratsiraka Returns to Power with Pro-Market Platform
notes: Confirmed. Ratsiraka won December 1996 election (second round December 29) with 50.7% of vote, took office February 1997.

title: Constitutional Referendum Strengthens Presidential Powers
notes: Confirmed. 1998 constitutional referendum approved strengthening of presidential powers and increased provincial autonomy.

title: Cyclone Hudah Destroys Antsiranana Region with 200 km/h Winds
notes: Cyclone Hudah struck April 2000 and caused major destruction. However, primary affected areas were Antalaha, Andapa, and Maroansetra in the northeast — not Antsiranana specifically. Death toll was approximately 111, not 'over 100.' The 200 km/h wind figure could not be confirmed. Broadly plausible but specific claims about Antsiranana and exact wind speed unverified.

title: Sapphire Rush Near Ilakaka Creates Boom-Town Economy
notes: Confirmed. Ilakaka sapphire rush is well-documented. Madagascar became world's leading sapphire producer. Environmental damage and value capture by intermediaries confirmed.

title: Disputed Election Creates Dual Government and Near Civil Conflict
notes: Confirmed. Disputed December 2001 election. Ravalomanana declared himself president February 2002. General strike, roadblocks, dual-government crisis confirmed.

title: Constitutional Court Rules for Ravalomanana, Ratsiraka Flees to Exile
notes: Confirmed. High Constitutional Court ruled for Ravalomanana. Ratsiraka fled to France. Crisis resolved.

title: Political Crisis Causes 13% GDP Contraction
notes: Confirmed. Real GDP dropped 12.7% in 2002, consistent with the stated ~13% figure.

title: Vanilla Price Crashes from $500 to Below $50 per Kilogram
notes: Confirmed. Vanilla peaked at ~$500/kg around 2003-2004, then collapsed to ~$40/kg by mid-2005 due to synthetic vanillin substitution and improved supply. The year and price range are broadly correct.

title: Durban Vision Commits Madagascar to Tripling Protected Areas
notes: Confirmed. Ravalomanana announced Durban Vision at World Parks Congress. Commitment to triple protected areas from 1.7 million to 6 million hectares confirmed.

title: Ambatovy Nickel and Cobalt Mine Project Announced
notes: Confirmed. Ambatovy project announced, led by Sherritt International. Investment projected over $5 billion. Largest single FDI in Madagascar's history.

title: Daewoo Land Deal Triggers Mass Outrage, Fuels Political Crisis
notes: Confirmed. November 2008 reports of 1.3 million hectare, 99-year lease to Daewoo Logistics. Triggered public outrage and contributed directly to 2009 coup. Deal cancelled by Rajoelina.

title: Military-Backed Coup Installs Rajoelina, Madagascar Suspended from AU
notes: Confirmed. Military transferred power to Rajoelina March 17, 2009. Madagascar suspended from both AU and SADC.

title: US and EU Suspend Hundreds of Millions in Aid After Coup
notes: Confirmed. US and EU suspended aid. AGOA trade preferences withdrawn. Garment sector devastated, factory closures, tens of thousands of jobs lost.

title: Post-Coup Rosewood Logging Crisis Devastates Northern National Parks
notes: Confirmed. Organized illegal rosewood logging operations in Marojejy and Masoala national parks after political collapse. Criminal networks exploited the vacuum; exports to China documented by Global Witness.

title: Garment Sector Collapses After AGOA Withdrawal, 40,000 Jobs Lost
notes: Confirmed. AGOA withdrawal caused garment sector collapse. ~40,000 workers lost jobs. Sector had employed over 100,000 at peak.

title: SADC Roadmap Agreement Charts Path Back to Constitutional Rule
notes: Confirmed. SADC-facilitated roadmap signed September 2011. Outlined path to inclusive transitional government and elections.

title: Presidential Elections Restore Constitutional Rule, End Transition
notes: Confirmed. Hery Rajaonarimampianina won 2013 election. International observers judged it broadly credible. Aid programs resumed.

title: Ambatovy Nickel Mine Begins Commercial Production
notes: Confirmed. Ambatovy reached commercial production January 2013. Nameplate capacity 60,000 tonnes nickel and 5,600 tonnes cobalt annually.

title: Cyclone Enawo Kills 81, Destroys 30% of Vanilla Crop
notes: Confirmed. Enawo struck March 7, 2017 as Category 4 equivalent (winds >225 km/h). 81 fatalities confirmed. ~30% vanilla crop damage confirmed by producers. Strongest storm since Gafilo 2004.

title: Urban Pneumonic Plague Outbreak Kills Over 200, Draws WHO Emergency Response
notes: Confirmed. 2,417 cases and 209 deaths by end of acute phase. Outbreak spread to urban centers. WHO deployed emergency response. 7,122 contacts received prophylactic antibiotics.

title: Presidential Election: Rajoelina Defeats Ravalomanana in Credible Runoff
notes: Confirmed. Rajoelina won December 19, 2018 runoff with 55.7%. Ravalomanana accepted result. Broadly judged credible by international observers.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Eliminates Tourism Revenue, Government Promotes Unproven Remedy
notes: Confirmed. COVID-19 destroyed tourism revenue. Rajoelina promoted Covid-Organics herbal remedy causing WHO diplomatic controversy. GDP contracted.

title: UN Declares First Climate-Driven Famine in Grand Sud Region
notes: The famine crisis is real but the year is imprecise. The crisis escalated in 2020-2021, with the UN making the 'first climate famine' declaration in 2021 (not 2020). World Weather Attribution also contested the 'solely climate-driven' framing. The event should be dated 2021.

title: Cyclone Batsirai Kills 121, Displaces 120,000 on Eastern Coast
notes: Confirmed. Batsirai made landfall February 5, 2022. 121 deaths confirmed. ~112,000 displaced. Fianarantsoa and Toamasina (Atsinanana) regions affected.

title: Rajoelina Re-elected in Opposition-Boycotted Controversial Election
notes: Confirmed. November 2023 election boycotted by major opposition. Rajoelina won 58.9%. French citizenship eligibility dispute confirmed. Low turnout (46.4%). SADC observers expressed concerns.

title: Political Opposition Organizes for Electoral Reform Ahead of Next Cycle
notes: Plausible continuation of post-2023 dynamics but specific 2025 events (SADC mediation, reform campaigns) could not be confirmed from available sources.
